_title: Fin:Track — Your money, calculated the Canadian way
_desc: Fin:Track tracks your TFSA, FHSA and RRSP contribution room, amortizes your mortgage with Canadian semi-annual compounding, and accrues credit line interest daily. In English and in French.
h1: How much TFSA room do you have left?
hsub: Your budgeting app knows your spending. It doesn't know your contribution room, it amortizes your mortgage the American way, and it has never heard of an FHSA. Fin:Track is built here, for the rules that apply here — in English and in French.
hnote: iOS 17 and later. English, French, Spanish, Portuguese.
f1s: No account needed to get started
f3s: Both complete, plus Spanish and Portuguese
f4s: For the rules that apply here
jp: These aren't details. The wrong compounding method skews your mortgage payment every single month, and one contribution too many costs 1% per month in penalty. The screens below come from the app.
e1h: Your contribution room, anchored to the CRA
e1p: You enter the room shown in CRA My Account once, with its reference year. Fin:Track then projects every contribution and every withdrawal — including the rule that catches everyone: a TFSA withdrawal only restores your room on January 1 of the following year.
e2p: In Canada, mortgage interest compounds twice a year, not twelve times. Apps built in the United States apply monthly compounding and get your payment wrong. Fin:Track uses the equivalent periodic rate, separates principal from interest, and counts the payments you have left.
e3h: Credit lines, at the daily rate
e3p: A Canadian line of credit accrues interest every day on the balance you have drawn. Fin:Track shows the daily rate to four decimal places, estimates the real monthly cost, tracks your utilization, and handles all three minimum payment types instead of assuming one.
ah: And everything else a real finance app needs
ap: Canadian precision is the reason to choose Fin:Track. Day to day, it still has to be complete.
cnote: Real screenshots taken on iPhone. The amounts belong to a fictional Quebec household used for the demo.

ph: Your data stays where it belongs
pp: A bank statement says where you live, where you eat, who you pay and when you were sick. Fin:Track is built so that information doesn't leave your device unless you ask it to.
p1p: Your data lives in the app, protected by the system's encryption. No sign-up is required to get started.
p2p: Syncing across your devices runs through your own private iCloud account, not through our servers.
p3p: It runs through a Canadian provider, it turns on only if you want it, and the app stays complete without it.
xh: Three tiers, one of them genuinely free
xp: What costs us nothing each month is paid for once. What carries a recurring cost — the bank connection, AI — is paid by subscription. Prices in Canadian dollars.
x0quoi: All the manual tracking, with no time limit.
x1quoi: The contribution room calculator and everything that costs nothing to run.
x2quoi: For those who want transactions to arrive on their own.
bh: The beta opens soon on TestFlight
bp: Leave your email and you'll get the invitation. Nothing else: no newsletter, no sharing with third parties.
bnote: You can opt out at any time.
fg1: Fin:Track is not affiliated with the Canada Revenue Agency or with any financial institution. The contribution room shown is a projection calculated from the amounts you enter: your official record remains CRA My Account.
fg2: Fin:Track does not provide financial, tax or investment advice. Screenshots show demonstration data.
